aiReview.summary: Google Research preprint on prompt-to-full-web-page Generative UI, with human preference results, the PAGEN expert-page dataset, and interactive demos. Useful as a primary paper, not a product or SDK you can run yourself.
evidence: Abstract and §2 describe HTML page generation plus tools, system instructions, and post-processors.
Tables 1–2: Generative UI ELO 1710.7 vs markdown 1459.6; 82.8% preference over markdown on LMArena sample.
§4 and discussion state PAGEN and demos are released for evaluation.
Listed from narrowin/awesome-generative-ui README as a paper PDF.
uncertainty: Whether PAGEN files and the live demo remain available and complete.
Reproducibility of the Google-internal tool server and Gemini backbone outside the paper.
aiReview.tagline: Research on LLMs generating full interactive web UIs
aiReview.description: Google Research paper showing LLMs can emit custom interactive pages, with preference studies, PAGEN, and public demo examples.
pros: Peer-style Google Research preprint with method, ablations, and human preference ELOs versus markdown, search, and expert sites.
Reports PAGEN, an expert-crafted prompt-to-website set intended for public comparison.
Points to interactive examples at generativeui.github.io rather than screenshots alone.
Documents limitations including slow generation and occasional HTML/JS/CSS errors.
cons: The listed URL is a PDF preprint under review, not a maintained generator, CLI, or library.
System prompts, tools, and PAGEN download mechanics are not fully specified in the candidate listing.
Preference results ignore generation latency, which the paper says can take a minute or two.

aiReview.summary: Official March 2024 Vercel post announcing AI SDK 3.0 streaming of React Server Components from LLMs, with code, FAQ, and demo/docs links. Strong primary source for generative UI, but it is an announcement article rather than a living generator or kit.
evidence: Canonical Vercel blog dated March 1, 2024 titled Introducing AI SDK 3.0 with Generative UI support.
Code samples use `render` from `ai/rsc` with `text` and `tools` mapping to RSC, including async generator yields.
FAQ states RSC APIs currently work in Next.js App Router and full `render` tool mapping with OpenAI, Mistral, and Fireworks firefunction-v1 at time of writing.
Discovered repeatedly from awesome-generative-ui README as a curated primary link.
uncertainty: Whether current AI SDK still exposes the same `render` API as shown in 2024 samples.
Long-term maintenance of sdk.vercel.ai demo and docs URLs.
aiReview.tagline: Stream React components from LLMs via RSC APIs
aiReview.description: Learn how to map LLM tool calls to streaming React Server Components for richer, interactive AI UIs beyond markdown chat.
pros: Explains associating LLM responses and OpenAI-compatible tools with streaming React Server Components, including a weather-tool example.
Links to a live demo and AI SDK documentation for the RSC generative UI APIs.
FAQ covers Next.js App Router requirements, LLM/function-calling support, and use with LangChain or LlamaIndex via streamable UI primitives.
cons: The URL is a dated blog post; APIs such as `ai/rsc` `render` may have changed since March 2024.
Generative UI APIs described here depend on React Server Components and Server Actions, not Pages Router.
It is documentation/announcement content, not a standalone UI generator or design-system kit.

aiReview.summary: Primary Google Research post on prompt-to-interactive UI (HTML/CSS/JS), with paper, demos, and product experiments in Gemini and Search AI Mode. Strong source for the generative-UI space, but it is research/product documentation rather than a standalone generator or design kit.
evidence: Blog dated November 18, 2025; paper title “Generative UI: LLMs are Effective UI Generators”; project page generativeui.github.io.
Rubric match: generative UI / prompt-to-UI research with working demos, not a Figma plugin listicle.
Canonical URL is research.google/blog; low malware/spam risk.
uncertainty: Whether PAGEN has been released since the post.
Current availability and quality of Gemini dynamic view / Search AI Mode outside the U.S.
Long-term maintenance of demo pages versus the blog itself.
aiReview.tagline: Research on on-the-fly interactive UIs from any prompt
aiReview.description: Explains how LLMs generate custom interactive pages, tools, and simulations, with a paper, demos, and product experiments.
pros: Official Google Research write-up with a linked paper and project page of demos.
Describes a concrete pipeline: Gemini 3 Pro, tools, system instructions, and post-processing to HTML/CSS/JS.
Reports human preference evaluations versus markdown LLM output, search results, and expert-made sites, plus a planned PAGEN dataset.
Tied to shipped experiments (dynamic view in Gemini; AI Mode in Search for some subscribers).
cons: Not an open generator, SDK, or design-system kit you can run independently.
Authors note generation can take a minute or more and outputs can be inaccurate.
Search AI Mode generative UI is limited to Google AI Pro/Ultra in the U.S. at publication.

aiReview.summary: Google Research post on generating teacher-vetted STEM practice simulations with generative UI, pedagogical guardrails, a public sample library, and a classroom pilot. Strong GenUI research evidence, but it is an education experiment rather than a general-purpose generator or design-system kit.
evidence: Canonical Google Research blog dated September 17, 2026 with authors Gal Elidan and Yael Haramaty.
Quick links to arXiv 2609.20738, research.google.com/p/learning-interactives, and edu.google.com/pilot.
States 30+ English STEM interactives generated by AI and reviewed by teachers; UK STEM teacher ratings and a 12-teacher US study (avg 8/10).
Generation uses self-correcting loops including agentic solvability checks in Chrome.
uncertainty: Long-term availability and maintenance of the sample library and pilot.
Whether custom generation will become publicly available outside Workspace for Education schools.
Independent reproduction of teacher ratings beyond the blog and tech report.
aiReview.tagline: Teacher-vetted GenUI STEM simulations from research
aiReview.description: Explains generating guided STEM simulations with pedagogical guardrails, a public sample library, arXiv report, and a Google for Education pilot.
pros: Describes a GenUI pipeline with instructional-design requirements, scaffolding, and iterative pedagogical guardrails.
Links a public sample library of 30+ teacher-reviewed STEM simulations and an arXiv tech report.
Includes teacher evaluation results and a Google for Education pilot path for custom generation.
Provides demo media and annotated interface examples of generated simulations.
cons: Public generation of arbitrary topics is limited to a pilot rather than an open self-serve generator.
Scope is education STEM simulations, not a reusable developer SDK or design-system kit.
Classroom learning-gain studies are described as forthcoming, not completed in the post.

aiReview.summary: Vendor blog that explains three generative-UI patterns (static AG-UI, declarative A2UI/Open-JSON-UI, open-ended MCP Apps) with code and a playground repo. Useful as a concept article, not a standalone generator or kit.
evidence: Canonical URL is a CopilotKit blog dated January 29, 2026 by Anmol Baranwal and Nathan Tarbert.
Meta and body define generative UI as runtime agent influence via A2UI, Open-JSON-UI, or MCP Apps, using AG-UI.
Links https://github.com/CopilotKit/generative-ui-playground and notes hosted playground retirement.
uncertainty: Could not fully verify remaining article sections after the first ~300 lines of the fetch.
Playground repo quality, license, and maintenance were not inspected.
CopilotKit commercial terms vs open-source AG-UI were not verified from this page.
aiReview.tagline: 2026 guide to agent-driven UI patterns and specs
aiReview.description: Explains static, declarative, and open-ended generative UI, with AG-UI, A2UI, Open-JSON-UI, MCP Apps, and a playground.
pros: Covers three control-vs-freedom patterns with named specs (AG-UI, A2UI, Open-JSON-UI, MCP Apps).
Includes concrete CopilotKit code (useFrontendTool) and links a GitHub playground implementing all three.
States the hosted playground is retiring and points readers to local code.
cons: Primary CTA is CopilotKit product/docs, so it is not a vendor-neutral survey.
Hosted demo is being retired; readers must run the playground locally.
Not a working generator or design-system kit by itself.
